candidates.change_summary: Return an AssertionPolicy with blockAssertion set to true (was false).
Return an AssertionPolicy with arbitrateViaEscalationManager set to true (was false).
Return an AssertionPolicy with discardOracle set to true (was false).
Return an AssertionPolicy with validateDisputers set to true (was false).
Return an AssertionPolicy with all flags set to true (was all false).
Change function to return false instead of true.
Change function to return whether disputeCaller equals the zero address (true only for zero address), altering observable return.
Change function to return whether the assertionId is non-zero (true only when assertionId != 0).
Change function to return the negation of the original (return !true -> false) but expressed as a negation of a comparison, i.e., disputeCaller != disputeCaller (always false).
Return true only when both assertionId and disputeCaller are non-zero; otherwise false.
Replaced the empty body returning nothing with a concrete return of int256(0).
Replaced the empty body with a return of int256(1) to change observable return value.
Replaced the empty body with a return that depends on the 'time' argument (casts time to int256) to make output vary with input.
Replaced the empty body with a return that depends on the first byte of ancillaryData (or 0 if empty) to change output based on ancillaryData.

Remove the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier from requestPrice so it can be called by any address (changes whether PriceRequestAdded can be emitted), by editing the function signature to drop the modifier.
Make requestPrice revert (by requiring false) so after a call it will not complete and no event/state change occurs.
Have requestPrice also call optimisticAsserter.requestPrice(...) (introduce an outward call) before emitting the event, which can change observable behavior if that call alters state or reverts.
Tighten the onlyOptimisticAsserter modifier to require msg.sender equals tx.origin as well, changing which callers can pass the guard and thus whether requestPrice can be called successfully.
Insert emitting an event recording the assertionId and assertedTruthfully, changing observable state via logs after callback.

Replace empty body with storing the last resolved assertion and its truth in a new private state via a dummy call to optimisticAsserter.getAssertion (causes different external behavior if optimisticAsserter call reverts or emits).
Tighten access check to require msg.sender equals owner-like address zero, changing whether onlyOptimisticAsserter allows calls and thus whether assertionResolvedCallback can be invoked.
